newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal, India begin cross-border movement talks.
newsitem.headline: Nepal, India begin cross-border movement talks.

text.p: Nepal and India began talks on Thursday on controlling illegal activities across their porous border, particularly smuggling and trafficking in arms, women and drugs, officials said.

"The meeting will discuss ways and means of checking the movement of undesirable elements across the borders and facilitating the movement of Indian and Nepali nationals," Nepali Foreign Secretary Kumar Gyawali told Reuters.
Nepal and India share a 1,500-km (937-mile) sub-Himalayan border that their citizens can freely cross under a 47-year-old treaty between the two South Asian neighbours.
Voluntary organisations say thousands of young Nepali girls are brought across the border every year and sold for as little as $4 to brothels in Bombay, India's commercial capital.
New Delhi says separatist activities of Kashmiri rebels are increasing in Nepal, where sophisticated plastic explosives bound for India were seized earlier this year.
Dozens of guerrilla groups have waged a separatist revolt in the Himalayan region of Kashmir since 1990. Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have died in insurgency-related violence.

India and Nepal pledged in June, during a visit to Kathmandu by Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral, that they would not allow their territories to be used for activities directed against each other.
